critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/components/PostComposer.jsx (thumbnail derivation): when a user uploads a video, thumbnail_url is derived by regex-stripping the extension: `res.secure_url.replace(/\.(mp4|mov|webm|m4v)$/i, '.jpg')`. Cloudinary rewrites the URL after upload (e.g. `/upload/f_mp4,vc_h264,q_auto/dog.mp4` is what the backend echoes back on GET), and while Cloudinary DOES generate a `.jpg` for any public video, extensions like `.avi`, `.mkv`, `.3gp`, `.mpg` are not covered — an .avi upload would send `thumbnail_url` still ending in `.avi`, which would 404. Prefer Cloudinary's poster URL (`cloudinary.url(publicId, { resource_type: 'video', format: 'jpg' })`) or ask backend to derive it.

/app/frontend/src/pages/PostDetail.jsx line 116: fallback `post.video_url && !post.image_url` — if a creator ever attaches BOTH an image_url and a video_url (backend allows it, CreatePostBody accepts both), the video is silently dropped from the detail page. Same fallback exists in Home.jsx PostCard. Consider rendering both, OR make CreatePostBody enforce XOR at the API layer.

/app/frontend/src/pages/PostDetail.jsx line 44: optimistic like uses `p.likes + (liked ? -1 : 1)` but that can go negative if the server has already reset the count concurrently. Minor — server-side `resp.likes ?? p.likes` reconciles, but the 0→-1 flash is possible if the button is double-tapped.

/app/frontend/src/components/PostComposer.jsx does not surface upload progress and disables the Post button only via `posting || uploading`; large video uploads to Cloudinary can take a while — consider a progress indicator on the preview card so users don't think it hung.

/app/backend/server.py CreatePostBody (line 122): all media fields are optional and there's no server-side XOR / minimum-content check. `POST /api/posts` with `{ caption: '' }` succeeds and creates an empty post (frontend guards against it but a direct API caller can litter the DB). Recommend `if not (caption.strip() or image_url or video_url): raise 400`.
